title: Security Review: Encryption & KMS (BYOK/HSM) - Orion Payments
summary: High-level security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit, customer-managed keys (BYOK), HSM options, and audit logging. Discussed implications for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments, key rotation, revocation, and integration requirements. Agreed to share SOC2 artifacts, HSM attestation docs, and a KMS integration diagram; schedule a technical follow-up to validate envelope encryption flow with Orion's security team.
topics: data residency and VPC/private deployment implications
RBAC/SSO integration and key access control
action_items: Sam Nguyen (Redwood AE): Send SOC 2 Type II report + compliance pack and link to security whitepaper (due: 2026-01-20)
Priya Patel (Redwood SE): Produce KMS integration diagram showing envelope encryption and where CMKs are used (due: 2026-01-19)
Ethan Miller (Redwood SE): Provide CloudHSM attestation/FIPS docs and KMIP integration notes (due: 2026-01-22)
Michael Chen (Orion): Share key rotation policy + compliance checklist and preferred HSM provider (due: 2026-01-23)
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts and KMS integration diagram
Schedule technical follow-up to do a walkthrough of envelope encryption flow with Orion's infra team (target week of 2026-01-26)
Customer to confirm whether they'll require BYOK import or external HSM (CloudHSM) integration for pilot
Agree pilot scope: dedicated pool with CMK + audit log retention for 90 days
transcript:
[00:00] Sam (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll go through encryption and key management - I'll hand to Priya for the technical bit but first quick introductions.
[00:12] Michael (Orion): Hi, Michael Chen here, head of security at Orion. Thanks.
[00:18] Sara (Orion): Sara Lopez, cloud architect.
[00:21] Tara (Orion): Tara Singh, compliance.
[00:24] Sam (Redwood): Great, Priya?
[00:26] Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah thanks, so agenda is encryption at rest and in transit, KMS options, BYOK and HSM, and audit logging. We'll also touch on dedicated/private deployment impacts.
[00:40] Michael: Quick context - Orion stores transaction metadata and some PII, regulated in EU and US, so we need keys under our control, full audit trails, and FIPS attestation ideally.
[00:52] Priya: Totally makes sense. For hosted API we support customer-managed keys via envelope encryption; Redwood stores encrypted objects but the Customer Master Key (CMK) can be either Redwood-managed or customer-managed (BYOK).
[01:08] Sara: When you say BYOK how does that work - do we upload keys, or do you connect to our KMS?
[01:15] Priya: Two common patterns: 1) Import a key material into Redwood's KMS backing — that has some limitations around import/export; 2) Integrate with an external KMS/HSM via standard APIs (KMIP or Cloud provider KMS) so Redwood calls your CMK to unwrap data keys. The latter is preferred for stricter control.
[01:36] Michael: So in the external KMS case, Redwood never sees the plaintext CMK?
[01:40] Ethan (Redwood): Correct — envelope encryption: Redwood holds data encrypted with a data key, that data key is itself encrypted (wrapped) by your CMK. Decryption requires a call to your KMS to unwrap, so Redwood never has access to the raw CMK.
[01:56] Tara: Is that compatible with CloudHSM or only cloud KMSs?
[02:01] Priya: We support CloudHSM-backed keys for AWS (CloudHSM) and you can also use Azure Key Vault with HSM-backed keys and Google Cloud KMS Cloud HSM. For on-prem HSMs we can integrate via KMIP or a proxy approach; we have customers that run a private connector.
[02:19] Michael: Any latency concerns? Our transactions are sensitive to tail latency.
[02:24] Sam: Good question. Typical flow: decryption path only needs a KMS unwrap on cache miss; we do aggressive KV/prefix caching and short-lived data-key cache so most tokens don't hit the KMS for every request. For hot paths we can use a dedicated pool close to customer region to keep latency down.
[02:43] Sara: How about rotation and revocation - if we rotate a CMK, do we have to re-encrypt everything?
[02:50] Priya: No — with envelope encryption the data keys remain the same until you choose to rewrap them; rotation can be done by rewrapping existing data keys with the new CMK or simply creating new data keys for new objects. Re-encryption of large backfills is optional but supported; we can automate a rewrap job.
[03:08] Michael: What happens if we revoke a key — can we instantly block access?
[03:12] Ethan: Yes, if you disable the CMK in your KMS, unwrap calls will fail and no new data keys can be unwrapped; existing cached data-keys in the runtime have TTLs so there's a small window, but you can configure TTLs to be short for stronger revocation. We'll document exactly where caches are and how to reduce that window.
[03:33] Tara: Audit logs — we need proofs of key usage and operator access logs for SOC 2 and audits.
[03:39] Priya: Redwood publishes detailed audit logs: key unwrap/requests, which Redwood identities initiated the call, region, IP, and request ids. For BYOK we also recommend combining Redwood logs with your KMS's own access logs so you get both sides of the story. We support pushing audit logs to S3/Cloud Storage or to your SIEM via streaming.
[04:01] Michael: Is the audit trail immutable?
[04:03] Ethan: We write append-only entries and we can set export to a customer-owned bucket with object lock / WORM to satisfy immutability requirements.
[04:11] Sara: Any certifications around HSMs? We need FIPS 140-2/140-3 and HSM attestation for CloudHSM.
[04:18] Priya: Cloud providers publish FIPS and Common Criteria attestations, and for CloudHSM we can provide attestation and the HSM vendor certs. For on-prem HSMs we'll ask for your attestation document; Redwood does not host the HSM hardware for BYO-HSM in private setups.
[04:35] Michael: What about key usage separation — who at Redwood can trigger unwraps?
[04:40] Sam: We have RBAC controls in the console and service accounts for runtime. Unwrap operations are performed by the runtime service identity; operator access is restricted. For audit we log human-initiated actions separately.
[04:54] Tara: Do you support SSO and SCIM for admin RBAC?
[04:58] Priya: Yes, SSO via SAML/OpenID Connect and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC roles map to least privilege roles; you can restrict key management actions to a small group.
[05:08] Michael: About data residency — can we ensure keys never leave our region?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes, you can provision CMKs in-region and Redwood's routing can be configured to route requests to in-region dedicated pools. For hosted customers we have region controls; for strict requirements we recommend dedicated or private deployment so that all runtime and KMS traffic stays within your VPC and region.
[05:30] Sara: Any network architecture docs? We need details on connections between Redwood runtime and customer KMS, firewall rules, and mutal TLS.
[05:37] Priya: We'll share a KMS integration diagram and a network runbook. We use mTLS for connections to customer-managed endpoints and recommend private endpoints (VPC peering or PrivateLink) where possible.
[05:49] Michael: Can Redwood use customer-provided HSM via a proxy in our VPC?
[05:53] Priya: Yes — we support a private connector that runs in your VPC, calls your on-prem HSM via KMIP or vendor APIs, and proxies unwrap requests. That keeps CMK operations inside your network.
[06:05] Tara: Is there a requirement for key escrow or split keys?
[06:09] Ethan: We can support split-key arrangements in the integration architecture — for example, using a multi-party HSM or having the CMK be derived, but that's a more bespoke setup and we'd want to scope it in a POC.
[06:21] Michael: What about encryption in transit specifics? Do you do TLS 1.3 only, cipher suites, cert rotation?
[06:27] Priya: We use TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred where supported. We publish our cipher suite list; certificates are rotated regularly and we support mutual TLS for private endpoints.
[06:37] Sara: Are there any pitfalls with model KV cache and encryption — could cache contain sensitive plaintext?
[06:42] Priya: Good callout — the KV/prefix cache stores ephemeral decrypted state in memory only in the runtime; we never write plaintext cache to disk. For stronger isolation we can pin certain tenant workloads to dedicated instances and enforce memory zeroization policies on eviction.
[06:58] Michael: What's the impact to cost and latency if we go to BYOK with external HSM?
[07:03] Sam: There's modest added latency on unwrap operations and additional egress for KMS calls. For most workloads the additional cost is KMS API usage and possibly CloudHSM-hourly charges. We can model this for your expected QPS and show delta in a cost worksheet.
[07:18] Tara: For SOC 2, auditors will want to see our cloud logs and Redwood's logs — how do we provide evidence?
[07:25] Ethan: We can provide exported logs, attestation docs, and a runbook demonstrating access controls. We'll also provide the SOC2 Type II report and ISO certs where available.
[07:34] Priya: Another note: if you require HSM-backed keys and FIPS validation for the entire stack, Private deployment with customer-managed HSM is the cleanest route — that gives you full control over the key lifecycle.
[07:47] Michael: For the pilot we want to test envelope encryption with our AWS KMS CMK and see unwrap times under load.
[07:54] Priya: We can set up a dedicated pool in us-east-1, configure Redwood to call your AWS KMS CMK, and run an unwrap latency benchmark. We'll include cache TTL settings.
[08:05] Sara: How will credentials be stored for the integration? Do we give Redwood an IAM role?
[08:09] Ethan: For AWS we recommend granting Redwood a cross-account IAM role with least privileges (kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey) and we provide an ARN to assume. For other clouds we use the analogous service accounts. For on-prem HSMs we use a connector with mTLS client certs.
[08:25] Michael: Any risks around compromise of the runtime instance leading to data key exposure?
[08:30] Priya: We treat that seriously: data keys are short-lived in-memory, we use hardware isolation on dedicated pools where possible, and enforce strict ASM/permissioning for operator actions. If you're most risk-averse, private deployment with your own HSM eliminates exposure of CMK.
[08:47] Sara: Are there limits on key sizes or supported algorithms? We use RSA for some legacy and prefer AES-GCM for data keys.
[08:54] Priya: We use AES-GCM/256 for data keys and support RSA/OAEP wrap for certain flows, but AES wrap and KMS-native mechanisms are standard. We'll send a crypto spec sheet.
[09:06] Tara: Any mis-transcription here — forgive me, I see 'ash-em' in notes earlier?
[09:11] Michael (laughs): Yeah I think the auto-transcript wrote 'ash-em' for HSM.
[09:15] Sam: Happens all the time.
[09:18] Priya: Next topic briefly: key lifecycle policy, backups, and geo-redundancy.
[09:24] Michael: For backups do you recommend exporting key material? We usually do not export root key material for compliance.
[09:29] Ethan: We recommend not exporting CMKs; instead rely on replicated KMS services or HSM clustering. For disaster recovery we can architect the runtime to failover and use region-specific CMKs.
[09:41] Sara: If we change to a new CMK in another region will old ciphertexts still be readable?
[09:46] Priya: You can rewrap older data keys with the new CMK as part of a migration job. Otherwise you'd need the old CMK to unwrap historical data.
[09:57] Michael: How does Redwood separate logs between customers? We need to ensure no cross-tenant log leakage.
[10:02] Priya: All logs are tenant-scoped and we provide per-tenant log streams. We have strict multi-tenancy separation and can export to your own storage for ultimate control.
[10:12] Tara: Are there any legal/process requirements for BYOK — e.g., key escrow for law enforcement?
[10:17] Sam: Redwood does not escrow customer keys. If you require key escrow, that's a bespoke legal and architecture conversation, and may change the threat model. We recommend capturing that in the contract.
[10:30] Michael: Anything else about HSM attestation we should know?
[10:33] Ethan: We'll share vendor attestation and, for CloudHSM, the cloud provider's compliance docs. If you need deeper attestation we can coordinate with your security team to schedule an architecture deep dive.
[10:45] Priya: I'll note one gotcha — when you do BYOK import into some KMSs, imported keys sometimes can't be exported and have different lifecycle semantics. We should confirm which mode you want: import or external KMS.
[10:58] Sara: I think we prefer external KMS via cross-account role to avoid key material import.
[11:03] Tara: How long will audit logs be retained? We need 12 months minimum, preferably 2 years for some regs.
[11:09] Priya: Redwood default audit retention is 90 days, but we offer add-ons for extended retention (6, 12, 24 months) and can stream logs to your archival storage for long-term retention.
[11:20] Michael: On the subject of SSO — if an admin is removed in our IdP, how quickly does console access revoke?
[11:26] Sam: SCIM provisioning can deactivate accounts almost immediately; session TTLs are configurable and we can force logout for revoked sessions.
[11:33] Sara: Any sample policy docs for least-privileged roles?
[11:36] Priya: Yes we'll include role templates and example IAM policies for cross-account access.
[11:41] Michael: For the pilot we'll need a simple checklist.
[11:44] Ethan: We'll create a pilot security checklist with steps for KMS, network, RBAC, and logging.
[11:50] Sam: OK wrapping up — to recap Redwood will send SOC2 report, KMS integration diagram, HSM attestation docs, and a pilot checklist. We'll propose a pilot with AWS KMS CMK and dedicated pool.
[12:03] Tara: Sounds good, thanks.
[12:05] Michael: Thanks everyone.
[12:07] Sam: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the week of Jan 26.
[12:11] (end)
